Meta provides a suite of built-in tools designed to help you connect with supporters and collect donations directly on the platform where they’re already spending their time. You have two main options for raising money: you can send people to your own website to give, or you can use Meta’s features to collect donations without ever asking supporters to leave the app.

At its heart, Facebook’s fundraising toolkit is about making giving easy. The most visible feature is the "Donate" button, which you can add to your Page header, individual posts, and even your Instagram profile. When someone clicks this button, you can direct them to your organization's donation website. Alternatively, you can set up on-platform fundraisers where supporters can give in just a few taps. This seamless experience is key for converting casual followers into active donors. These tools are the starting point for building deeper connections, which you can then nurture through channels like direct messaging. Finally, your organization must be based in an eligible country, which includes the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia. Good — found something concrete, and it's important enough that I want to flag it clearly rather than keep troubleshooting menus: **Meta's fundraising/donation tools specifically require you to be a registered 501(c)(3)** organization, enrolled through PayPal Giving Fund, to get the Donate button and nonprofit fundraising features.

TMI is a 508(c)(1)(a), not a 501(c)(3) — and per what I know, that was a deliberate structural choice you made. That distinction may be the actual wall here, not a UI setting you haven't found yet. Meta's system checks entity type for those specific features, and 508(c)(1)(a) organizations don't automatically get the same recognition Meta's nonprofit tools are built around, since Meta explicitly built that pathway for 501(c)(3)s.

**What's separate from that, and doable regardless of entity type:**
In Business Settings → Business Info, there's a general "business type" field where you can categorize the Portfolio as Nonprofit/Organization — this affects how the Page is categorized and may open some general nonprofit-labeled features, but it is not the same gate as the Donate button/fundraising tools application at facebook.com/donate/signup, which is the one tied to the 501(c)(3)/tax-ID discount you're after.

So the honest picture: setting your business type correctly is a small, doable fix. Getting the actual tax-ID-linked nonprofit ad discount and donation tools may require either applying anyway and seeing what Meta's verification actually asks for (since I can't rule out 508(c)(1)(a) working — I haven't found a source that explicitly excludes it), or it genuinely being blocked by entity type, in which case that's a structural fact about Meta's program, not something we can UI our way around.
